title: Judicial-grade audit ledger with HSM timestamping and WORM evidence exports
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Goal: Provide a tamper-evident, legally-defensible audit ledger for admin actions (privileged access, config changes, RBAC adjustments) that meets strict evidence requirements for regulated customers. The ledger must be append-only, cryptographically anchored, time-stamped via HSM/KMS-backed attestation, and produce WORM-compliant export bundles with provenance metadata and residency labels.

Scope:
- Capture admin API events, console actions, and internal operator operations with structured context (actor, target, delta, request_id, region).
- Stream events into an append-only ledger service that writes to immutable blobs and produces periodic signed manifests.
- Integrate HSM-based timestamps (notarization) to provide an independent time attestation for each epochal checkpoint.
- Offer an export API to produce sealed evidence bundles (WORM) for a given retention horizon and region, with optional escrow hooks and legal-hold flags.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement full multi-tenant legal workflows (separate ticket planned). It focuses on ledger mechanics, attestation, and export shapes.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) End-to-end flow for admin_action -> ledger write -> HSM checkpoint -> sealed export exists in staging.
2) Audit entries include canonical residency tag and retention label.
3) Export bundles are verifiable: each bundle includes a manifest.json, ledger checkpoint signature, and per-blob SHA256 checksums.
4) Latency and SLO: median additional latency for admin API calls < 8ms for synchronous write path (best-effort), and < 50ms P99; streaming/async path documented.
5) Unit/integration tests for tamper-detection, signature verification, and region-filtered exports.

Design notes & trade-offs: 
- Two-path write model: (A) fast async append to a local WAL then background commit to immutable blobstore; (B) optional sync path for high-assurance customers where write awaits HSM-anchored checkpoint. Trade-off: lower throughput and higher latency for sync path vs stronger immediate attestation.
- HSM integration: we will use existing KMS-HSM bridge (KMS providers with HSM-backed signing) to minimize infra operational burden. Alternative (building our own notary cluster) was rejected due to time and complexity.
- Residency: every ledger entry must carry region_id, data_residency_policy, and a derived residency_bucket path so that export bundles can be segregated by legal jurisdiction.
- Storage: use object store lifecycle with write-once buckets (cloud provider immutability flags) where supported + signed manifests. For on-prem customers, provide a local WORM agent that flips immutable bit via vendor API.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (staging): implement ingestion and local append-only WAL + background blob commit.
- Week 2 (staging): wire HSM timestamping on epochal checkpoints and emit signed manifests.
- Week 3 (canary): export bundle generation + verification tooling; run canary in two regions.
- Week 4 (prod): enable opt-in sync path and offer sealed-export endpoint to security team for review.

Monitoring & observability:
- New metrics: ledger_write_latency_ms, checkpoint_sign_time_ms, export_bundle_size_bytes, export_generation_duration_ms, export_verification_failures_total.
- Dashboards: per-region retention compliance view and proof-generation success rate.
- Alerts: export_verification_failures_total > 0.5% over 15m, HSM_sign_rate_drop > 3 sigma.

Security & compliance considerations:
- Keys used for signing timestamps are HSM-protected and rotated per policy; access to signing keys is restricted to the notary service principal.
- Audit records contain only metadata about actions; sensitive payloads are redacted via existing redaction pipeline before persistence.
- Legal-hold: exports must be able to override retention deletion; manifests will include legal_hold=true flag when present.

Docs & artifacts: 
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPLIANCE/Judicial-Grade-Audit-Ledger
- Architecture diagram: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/ledger-arch-2025
comments: 2025-03-01: Ticket created by Aisha. Initial scope and acceptance criteria defined.
2025-03-03: Spike completed for WAL->immutable-blob pipeline. Found that cloud provider immutability APIs have heterogeneous semantics; implementing an abstraction layer.
2025-03-05: Design review with Security and Legal. Legal asked for manifest schema that includes operator justification and case_id when applicable.
2025-03-07: Implemented HSM signing prototype using existing KMS integration (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2789). Verifier code added to staging toolchain.
2025-03-09: Performance testing: sync HSM path increases P99 write latency ~120ms on staging under load. Decided to gate sync path behind customer opt-in and circuit-breaker thresholds.

2025-03-11: QA found intermittent checksum mismatch on large export bundles (>1GB). Root cause: chunk boundary ordering during parallel commit. Patch in progress (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-ledger/pull/412).
2025-03-12: Marco: documenting migration plan for existing audit data into new ledger format and coordinating with SRE for storage bucket immutability flags.
Next steps: finalize manifest schema with Legal, land checksum fix, run two-region canary, and open security review docket.
